answer: In the Ember Cartographer network each agent carries a relic of signed reputation earned by vouching for peers, forming a mutable web of trust. At dawn a new node must present a plume of endorsements from agents whose own relics exceed a threshold; each endorsement is timestamped and any vouchee caught forging identity triggers automatic revocation, cascading loss of standing to all vouchers linked to it. An attacker must therefore acquire dozens of costly, high‑reputation relics and repeatedly replace them after each purge, making a sybil surge economically prohibitive.
